items: Daniel's faithfulness in prayer is central to the story in Daniel 6.
The Book of Job explores innocent suffering and challenges simplistic explanations for hardship.
The Beatitudes appear in Matthew 5:1–12 and in a related form in Luke 6:20–26.
Jesus teaches the Lord's Prayer in Matthew 6:9–13 and Luke 11:2–4.
Zacchaeus' response to Jesus includes practical restitution, not only regret (Luke 19:1–10).
Acts 10 tells how Peter's encounter with Cornelius challenges inherited boundaries of inclusion.
The early Christian community is described as sharing resources so that people in need are cared for (Acts 4:32–35).
First Corinthians 13 places love at the centre of Christian gifts and service.
Nehemiah combines prayer with planning and shared work in rebuilding Jerusalem's walls.
In the parable of the Good Samaritan, Jesus makes neighbour-love visible through practical care.
John 4 shows Jesus crossing social boundaries in his conversation with a Samaritan woman.
Revelation 21 offers a vision of God dwelling with humanity and bringing comfort to those who mourn.
The Christian liturgical year begins with Advent in the Roman Rite, though dates and practices can differ in local calendars.
The Catholic Bible contains 73 books; editions in other Christian traditions may use a different canon.
Scripture quotations in apps should be accompanied by a translation name and checked against permissions for digital redistribution.
